description: Lending-specific and collections/risk platform vendors (e.g. nCino, Provenir, CRIF, Experian, FIS, SBS/Sopra) were not systematically searched against Slovenian institutions in this pass.

The SI institution keyword list used here covered NLB, OTP banka (ex Nova KBM/SKB), Gorenjska banka, Addiko, Delavska hranilnica, Sparkasse, BKS, UniCredit and Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, but not the full set of savings banks, the leasing arms, or the Slovene subsidiaries' group-level IT decisions taken in Vienna/Budapest/Milan.
Global vendors' regional implementation-partner networks (the unnamed 'local vendor' credited in the NLB/Temenos R17 upgrade) were not identified.
All candidates in this slice were discovered via search-result metadata; no page was fetched and confirmed in-session, so page-level content claims rest on search summaries.
The card management / issuing platform layer under Bankart and under SI banks is unmapped — no named CMS, switch, HSM or tokenisation supplier identified.
No recruitment/job-posting sources were collected, though these are among the most reliable public indicators of which payment platforms an organisation actually operates.

Conference and industry-association sources for SI payments (Bančni vestnik, Združenje bank Slovenije, ICT/payments conferences) were not covered; these carry vendor presentations naming implementations.
Cross-border consolidation (Nexi Croatia owning Nexi Slovenija; NLB's regional footprint) means SI vendor facts often appear only in HR/RS/BA sources.
No candidate URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed; all liveness assessments are search-result-derived only.
EU-level tender data (TED) and ECB/ESCB oversight publications on SI payment infrastructures were not directly scouted.

Sponsor and exhibitor rosters are typically deleted or replaced when a conference site rolls to the next edition. DSI is the exception (per-year subdomains 2021-2026); Money Motion partly (year subdomains); most others keep only the current edition.
Sponsor tiers on Money Motion, INFOSEK and DSI are rendered as logo images, sometimes without informative alt text, so plain HTML scraping will under-recover vendor names.
NT konferenca, CIO Summit and WEBSI were reached only via a media calendar or press coverage; their canonical organiser domains were not confirmed in this pass.

The highest-signal Slovenian payments gathering (ZBS posvetovanje o kartičnem poslovanju) is a member consultation whose detailed agenda may not be published openly; only a descriptive blurb was found.

Only Money Motion was covered on the regional axis. Other Adriatic/CEE payments and banking events that Slovenian banks attend (e.g. Croatian, Serbian and Austrian banking/cards conferences) were not enumerated.
No social-listening source was recorded for conference attendance, which in practice is where Slovenian vendor and bank staff self-declare presence at events (booth photos, 'we are at X' posts).

Only DIGGIT was confirmed to have an explicit financial-services/insurance/banking award category. Whether WEBSI, Netko and GZS innovation awards carry a finance-specific category was not established.
No licensed access path established to the two paywalled cornerstones of this cell: Casnik Finance (finance.si, Moje finance, Manager) and the STA wire.
Only current-web coverage was reached; no Slovenian newspaper archive (Delo/Dnevnik/Vecer digital archives, Digitalna knjiznica Slovenije dLib) was explored for historical bank-IT supplier reporting.

Non-Ljubljana outlets (Vecer in Maribor, regional business weeklies) and RTVSLO's business desk were not covered in this pass; regional banks and savings banks (hranilnice) are typically covered there rather than nationally.

Slovene procurement/technology vocabulary for this domain was only partially exercised - terms not yet searched include 'javno narocilo', 'razpis', 'izvajalec', 'sistemski integrator', 'procesni center', 'karticno poslovanje', 'POS terminali', 'jedrni bancni sistem', 'zaledni sistem'.
Much of the freely accessible Slovenian IT trade content (Racunalniske novice, SRC InfoSRC) is vendor-supplied advertorial, but no method is yet defined for separating editorial from paid placement.

General newswires that carry vendor press releases verbatim (Business Wire, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, EIN Presswire) were not searched in this run, yet they are the origination point for many vendor announcements later picked up by Finextra/FinTech Futures.
Slovenian-language querying in this cell produced no vendor-selection news; the sl anchors used may be wrong rather than the content absent.

Actor map for this cell is anchored on NLB, Bankart, SID Banka and SKB/OTP only; other Slovenian banks (NKBM/OTP, Addiko, Delavska hranilnica, Gorenjska banka, Sparkasse, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, N Banka) and vendors (Halcom, Actual I.T., Comtrade, Iskratel/S&T-Kontron) were not systematically searched against the trade press.
The two highest-value systematic sources (SeeNews full wire, IBSi Sales League Table) are subscription products; free-tier monitoring will only yield headlines.
Analyst/consultancy channels that publish vendor-win data (Retail Banker International / GlobalData, The Banker's technology awards and rankings, Celent/Forrester vendor reports) were not covered.

PSD2/developer portals not yet pinned for several SI ASPSPs: Nova KBM/SKB legacy entities post-OTP merger, LON (Hranilnica LON), Primorska hranilnica Vipava, N26/Revolut-style non-bank PSPs operating in SI, and BKS Bank SI.

No technical fingerprinting layer defined yet (TLS certificate SANs, HTTP response headers, JS bundle vendor strings, mobile app binary/SDK inspection) — the highest-yield way to read a vendor off a portal that names no vendor.
Job ads and app release notes are ephemeral; nothing in the current source set guarantees historical retention.
Local-language searching was performed throughout, but no glossary yet exists for the SI-specific terms for card/ATM processing roles and core-banking modules, which limits recall on job boards.
LinkedIn — probably the richest weak-signal source for this cell — is login-walled and ToS-restricted, so systematic collection is not permissible by scraping.
No dedicated source identified for ownership changes at small SI payments/fintech vendors (ISV, POS, core-banking integrators) that fall below merger-notification and takeover thresholds.
No structured historical archive of AVK decisions older than the current web listing was located (archive depth unverified).
Group-level acquirer/processor deals (Nexi, Worldline, Nets, Erste, Intesa, UniCredit) affecting Slovenia are only partly covered by the parent-newsroom sources listed.
Several URLs (AVK news index, ATVP permit lists, MGTŠ FDI pages, NLB IR) were inferred or taken from search results rather than fetched in this run.

The Bankart open-banking endpoint (openbanking.bankart.si) is only known second-hand, from ATMinfo.si's footer attribution. Its actual structure, access requirements and field set were not established in this pass.

Glory Global Solutions - a major cash-recycling and teller-cash-automation competitor named in the cell brief - produced no Slovenian evidence at all, neither a country presence nor a local distributor.

Cash-in-transit and cash-management companies (e.g. Varnost, Sintal, G4S-successor operations in Slovenia) were not investigated, yet they are the operational counterparties for ATM cash replenishment, smart safes and recycling economics, and frequently co-bid or co-deliver with hardware vendors.

Posta Slovenije was identified as a named cash-point obligor in the draft cash-access law but was not researched as a buyer of self-service and cash equipment. Unlike commercial banks, it is a state-owned entity and therefore likely a contracting authority publishing tenders.

No visual/physical identification source was established for determining which ATM makes and models are actually deployed at Slovenian sites - the most reliable way to attribute installed base when neither banks nor vendors disclose it.
The Bankart annual report located is the 2019 edition; more recent annual reports and their ATM-count and partner disclosures were not retrieved.

This pass covered Hrc, Halcom, ZZI, SRC, Bankart, Comtrade SI, Špica, Genis, Mikrografija, Agitavit, IN516HT, Comland and Endava SI, but the domestic supplier population is larger. Not yet checked: Kontron/S&T Slovenija, Unistar LC, NIL/Conscia, Astec, Intech-LES, Datalab, Comtrade adjacent entities, CREA, Trilab, Optiweb-class digital agencies, and SI fintech/paytech startups.

No job-advertisement source was captured. SI job ads (Optius, MojeDelo, LinkedIn, vendor career pages) routinely name the client bank, the core platform and the technology stack — often the only public disclosure of a private bank's vendor.

The official Slovenian public-procurement portal (Portal javnih naročil / eJN, enarocanje.si) was not directly reached — only the si.openprocurements.com aggregator. Also unreached: AJPES as the authoritative registry and annual-report source (used indirectly via bizi/companywall).

No vendor PARTNER page (as opposed to customer reference page) was captured in this pass. Partner/technology-alliance pages are the mechanism by which a domestic integrator reveals the foreign platform behind an unnamed bank deal — the explicit rationale for this cell.

Several recorded URLs were surfaced via search-result metadata rather than fetched in this pass (Halcom support FAQ pages, hrc.si individual news article URLs, marand.si, in516ht.com, mikrografija.com/references/, gzs.si KATALOGI). Only hrc.si/si/o-nas was actually fetched.

Slovenian-language search was used throughout and was decisive (Hibis/Hrc, Bankart, ZZI and the ZBS/GZS pointers were only found via sl queries). However, no Serbian/Croatian-language searching was done even though Hrc, Halcom and Comtrade all operate HR/RS units whose local sites often name clients the SI sites omit.
flik.si was not crawled directly in this pass; its participant list, merchant/acquirer pages and any technical documentation remain unmapped.

Slovenian payments-adjacent operators and vendors not covered here: Halcom (e-banking/payments software), Bankhub/Bankart competitors in acquiring, Nexi/Nets local presence, Mastercard/Visa SI country offices, and Trgovinska/POS acquirers. These sit at the boundary of the cell but were not searched.
The BSI 'upravljavci placilnih sistemov' register and the BSI publications index were identified from search snippets but not fetched, so their actual content and update cadence are unknown.
No archival/temporal source was established for these sites (e.g. Wayback snapshots of bankart.si service pages or flik.si participant lists), so historical change detection would start from zero.

Slovenian business/financial media (Delo, Finance.si, Racunalniske novice interviews) were only touched incidentally; they are the main channel where Bankart executives discuss roadmap and vendor choices.
Crypto/e-money actors beyond Eligma/GoCrypto (e.g. Bitstamp's Slovenian origins, local exchanges and stablecoin/CASP entrants) were not enumerated from any licensed-entity list.

No developer/integration documentation portals (API docs, plugin repos, e-commerce platform marketplaces) were captured for Slovenian PSPs and wallets, despite being public by design and highly diagnostic of capability.
Merchant case studies and reference stories were largely absent; only press-reported partnerships (Petrol–mBills, VALÚ acceptance network) were found.
Core Slovenian business/financial media that most likely carry PSP deal news — Finance.si, STA, Ekipa/Svet kapitala, Poslovni dnevnik — were not confirmed as sources in this pass.
No quantitative payment-statistics source was captured for sizing non-bank share (card/instant payment volumes by instrument).
Newsrooms not yet located for UniCredit Banka Slovenija, BKS Bank AG branch Slovenia, Banka Sparkasse, Hranilnica LON, and the SDH/SID-owned institution perimeter beyond SID banka itself.
The cell explicitly covers SID/SDH-owned institutions, but SDH's own portfolio disclosures and SID banka's annual reports and procurement notices were not searched in this run.
Pre-merger announcement history for Nova KBM, SKB banka, Abanka and Sberbank/N Banka is not secured; current newsrooms only show the surviving brand.

Slovenian banks jointly consume shared national rails — Bankart (processing), Flik (instant P2P/merchant payments), SI-PASS and Rekono (eID) — repeatedly named in bank notices, but the operators' own newsrooms were not scouted in this cell.
No RSS/Atom feeds or sitemap endpoints were confirmed for any of the bank newsrooms in this run; all collection assumptions are HTML-crawl based.

Bank annual reports and Pillar-3/operational-risk sections routinely describe IT programmes, outsourcing arrangements and material service providers — far more explicitly than press releases — and were not collected.

Google Play and App Store listings for NLB Klik, DH Mobilni, mDBS, OTP and Gorenjska banka apps carry dated release notes, publisher metadata and sometimes SDK-revealing detail — the most granular buyer-side go-live evidence available.

Local-language querying was performed throughout and was clearly productive, but for the smallest hranilnice the Slovenian vocabulary that would surface technology news ('prenova', 'nadgradnja', 'nov informacijski sistem', 'zamenjava bančnega sistema') was only partially exercised.
No CPV code list was assembled for banking, payment, card, ATM, cash-in-transit and core-banking-IT categories in the SI context.

Municipal and other state-owned contracting authorities (Mestna občina Ljubljana and other občine, DARS, Slovenske železnice, health/university institutions, Zavod za pokojninsko in invalidsko zavarovanje) were not individually enumerated as buyers of payment/cash services.
Evidenčna naročila (below-threshold purchases) are not published as award notices, so a notice-only pipeline will underestimate vendor footprint and long-tail terminal/maintenance spend.
No archival/mirror strategy was identified for tender documentation that the portal removes after deadlines; only an unreliable third-party corpus (Lawinsider) surfaced.
Winning bidders appear under varying legal names and consortium forms; no company-register linkage was established in this pass.
The exact live URL of the SI CASP (crypto-asset service provider) authorisation list maintained by ATVP under MiCA was not pinned down; only the MiCA leaflet and the register index were confirmed.

AML-side registers were not searched: the Urad RS za preprecevanje pranja denarja (Office for Money Laundering Prevention) and the AJPES-held Register dejanskih lastnikov (beneficial ownership register) were not covered in this run.

The register of menjalci (money changers) and the register of payment system operators (upravljavci placilnih sistemov) are known to exist as filters in the BSI master register, but their dedicated sub-register URLs were not individually resolved.
No confirmed machine-readable feed (API, CSV, XML) was identified for the Banka Slovenije registers themselves; only the AJPES/OPSI business register has a confirmed open bulk file.

Cross-border passporting lists are effectively English-only at EU level (EBA/ECB/ESMA), while the SI-side lists are Slovenian-only, and entity names are transliterated/abbreviated inconsistently between them (d.o.o., d. o. o., d.d.).
No historical/archived snapshots of these registers were identified, so licence entries and withdrawals that occurred before collection starts are invisible.
Bilateral chambers of the ownership countries of Slovenian banks — Italian (Intesa Sanpaolo), Austrian (Sparkasse, BKS, Addiko), Hungarian (OTP), French (SKB/OTP legacy) — were not enumerated.

Association EVENT and CONFERENCE programme archives (ZBS Izobraževalni center, GZS/ZIT events, AmCham committee events) were identified conceptually but not systematically harvested; these are where bank–vendor working relationships and case studies are exposed.
No credible Slovenian-language term for a domestic 'fintech association' surfaced; the local vocabulary in this space is dominated by 'veriga blokov / blockchain' and 'digitalizacija', not 'fintech'.
Access status (open vs. member-gated) is unconfirmed for AHK Slovenija's member directory and for the AmCham full member list beyond the landing page.

Craft/SME chamber (OZS – Obrtno-podjetniška zbornica Slovenije), startup ecosystem bodies (Tehnološki park Ljubljana, Start:up Slovenija) and clusters outside ICT were not searched, although they list small software suppliers.
